lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' camp has already sorted out its first real battle line - grit versus comfort - and the veteran got squeezed. Steven Lorentz was placed on waivers, clearing room for Zack MacEwen to muscle into the fourth-line picture; that is a hard, plain message from management about what they want at the bottom of the lineup. Toronto is in the deep offseason, the season is over, and the club has to build from a clean slate after a year that left no margin for softness. The goaltending picture is still murky, too - Daily Faceoff's 18th-place ranking is a polite warning, not a compliment. MacEwen's bite and Joshua's size give this roster a different edge, but depth must prove it can score and survive. Next comes camp cuts, waiver churn, and the first true test of whether this group is tougher - and better - than the one it just left behind.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The winter arrives with one loud note still hanging in the air - George Springer is staring at the end of his Blue Jays deal, and he's not pretending otherwise. Springer's future is the headliner after a season that left Toronto with a final 74-88 record, and the club now has to decide whether to let a respected veteran walk, extend him, or turn the DH chair over to younger legs. The front office has already signaled where the holes are: the outfield, the lineup's thump, and a roster that needs more certainty than hope. Springer's.251 average and 15 homers tell the story of a bat that still mattered, even if the body has started collecting its due. What matters next is whether Toronto uses this offseason to buy power, protect the rotation, and build a cleaner path to camp.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet doesn't mean empty in Toronto; it means the board is being cleared for a new hand. Tyreke Key and Nimari Burnett were signed to Exhibit 10 deals, with AJ Hoggard waived - the sort of late-September housekeeping that tells you camp is coming fast and spots are still open. Bobby Webster also slapped down the ghosts of 2019, saying this group should keep moving forward, not keep staring in the rearview mirror. That's the right instinct. Immanuel Quickley is the hinge here, the guard who has to turn all this talent into something that looks like a rotation, not a scrapbook. Toronto's season is over, but the work isn't; the final record frames the urgency, not the obituary. Next comes camp, and the real test is whether the roster can harden into something larger than name recognition.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The biggest thing hanging over Ashburn is not a depth-chart debate - it's Jayden Daniels' left elbow, and Adam Peters just poured cold water on the worst fears. Surgery is not on the table and injured reserve hasn't been discussed, a small mercy for a franchise trying to keep its young quarterback upright while the medical opinions pile up. This is the kind of September that forces a sober front office to think in weeks, not headlines. The Commanders' offseason now feels less like housekeeping than triage, with Daniels' health dictating everything that comes next. Daronte Jones knows the other side of the ball still needs sanding down, especially the pass defense. The final record is a reminder of how thin the margin is; the real work is protecting the investment. What to watch now: Daniels' recovery timeline and whether Washington answers it with caution, depth, or a roster move.

article.title: Friday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs open camp with depth pressure, and MacEwen is fighting for Lorentz's job while Dakota Joshua is a player to watch as the season nears. The Blue Jays note George Springer is facing the end of his deal, with his Toronto run down to its final days.

The Raptors are still in deep offseason mode, with Immanuel Quickley framed as their most important piece and the bigger push being to move forward. In Washington, Commanders GM Adam Peters said Jayden Daniels is not headed for surgery or injured reserve after the elbow injury, and Marcus Mariota is set to start against Seattle.
